#915. Complaint filed to IRS in relation to Fifa head Gianni Infantino’s housekeeper

It calls for inquiry into claims she was on Fifa payroll

Fifa: Infantino personally pays for ‘any domestic staff’

A complaint has been filed to the United States Internal Revenue Service calling for an investigation into claims an individual on the Fifa payroll was working privately as a housekeeper for Gianni Infantino.

If the IRS investigates and finds the claims to be proven then Fifa could lose its tax-exempt status in the US. Fifa has 501(c)(4) status in the country, a category for organisations “created to promote community welfare for charitable, educational or recreational purposes”.

The complaint, which has been seen by the Guardian and is supported by a number of documents, claims an individual “performed domestic work exclusively for Fifa president Gianni Infantino and his wife, Leena Infantino, at their Miami residence, while receiving compensation or benefits through a Fifa-affiliated entity”, and argues that “senior leadership, acting in their official capacity and on behalf of Fifa, have abused the entity’s tax-exemption status”.

In the Guardian app, tap the Profile settings button at the top right, then select Notifications. Turn on sport notifications.

If you already have the Guardian app, make sure you’re on the most recent version.

If you don't have the Guardian app, download it from the iOS App Store on iPhone or the Google Play store on Android by searching for 'The Guardian'.

The complaint goes on to argue: “If organisational funds or resources were used to pay for services benefiting a leader’s household, the arrangement raises serious questions about private benefit, financial reporting, compensation, and governance. The materials also raise questions about the accuracy of representations in employment, payroll, tax, and immigration records. We ask the agencies to investigate the underlying records and determine what occurred.” The IRS has been approached for comment.

The news comes as Fifa’s activities, and specifically Infantino’s involvement in the failed Fifa Forward Enterprise (FFE) scheme and his relationship with the Trump White House, are to come under intensified scrutiny from Democratic politicians in the US after the “blue wave” at the midterm elections. A spokesperson for the ranking member of the House judiciary committee, representative Jamie Raskin, said the committee had not requested documents related to the housekeeper but was “looking closely at those developments”.

A Fifa spokesperson said: “Matters related to the Fifa president’s personal and home life are private; however, for the avoidance of any doubt, the costs of any domestic staff are met by the Fifa president personally.”

The complaint, if taken up, would probably take months to complete and commonly the results of IRS investigations are not published. Any action taken as a result, however, would be in the public domain. The complaint was submitted by the Washington DC lawyer Abed Ayoub, who works in immigration law and has served as the national executive director of the American-Arab Anti-Discrimination Committee (ADC). Last year the ADC was part of the campaign Game Over Israel, which called for Israeli football teams to be banned from international competition.

Fifa said: “We urge the media to act responsibly. As Fifa stated in August, it is evident that there is a concerted and ongoing effort by some to undermine Fifa and its president. Fifa welcomes legitimate scrutiny. But scrutiny is not a licence to amplify false allegations. Where reporting is inaccurate or misleading Fifa will continue to challenge it directly and vigorously.”

Infantino has been described by his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, as a “dictator” who “no longer knows any borders”. Blatter, Fifa’s president for 17 years before resigning amid a corruption scandal at the organisation, made the remarks in an interview with the German magazine Der Spiegel. He criticised the FFE scheme, the Fifa peace prize and, most significantly in his opinion, the overturning of Folarin Balogun’s suspension for a red card during the World Cup.

Our picture editors select their favourite sporting images from the past week, from the spectacular to the powerful, and with a little bit of fun thrown in

“Fifa is suffering,” Blatter said. “It is currently led by a person who has allowed himself to be blinded.” He described the peace prize as “embarrassing”, saying: “Why would he do something like that? Infantino awards a peace prize to someone who wages war against Iran shortly afterwards?”

In assessing the FFE scheme, which was abandoned after an international outcry, Blatter said: “Infantino no longer knows any borders. He doesn’t understand any of this.” He described the Balogun controversy as “the worst”, saying: “Statutes can be interpreted. But rules of the game must apply to everyone, you can’t interpret them.”

#914. England's Blues brothers - how the Bellinghams helped save Birmingham

Jude Bellingham shared an old photo of him and brother Jobe after England's squad announcement last week

It is six years since Jude Bellingham played his final game for Birmingham City, and three years since younger brother Jobe wore the club's shirt for the last time.

While Jude, 23, is establishing himself as a footballing great at European greats Real Madrid following a spell at Borussia Dortmund, Jobe, 21, is continuing his football education at his brother's former club in Germany after two seasons with Sunderland.

The Stourbridge-born midfielders have moved on with their careers.

Their memories, however, live on at St Andrew's, such was the impact the boyhood Birmingham fans made in the Championship.

On match days supporters stop and pose for photographs in front of Jude's mural outside the ground. Fans still turn up to matches wearing Bellingham shirts.

"They both had a real connection with fans," Craig Courtney, from the Tilton Talk fan podcast, told BBC Sport. "Fans loved the fact they both cared.

"They wore their hearts on their sleeves and helped Birmingham when we were fighting relegation. Even now, Jude and Jobe remember where it all started for them."

The brothers played 70 league and cup games between them for Birmingham after graduating from the academy.

They have never appeared together in a senior match, however, as Jude - who joined Birmingham aged eight - had left by the time Jobe broke into the first team in 2022.

The Bellinghams will become the first brothers to play for England for 19 years if Jobe wins his first cap and appears alongside Jude, a veteran of 60 appearances, in the Nations League game with Croatia at Wembley.

"It will be an incredibly proud moment for Birmingham City if that happens," said Courtney.

'A beautiful story' as Bellingham brothers called up

Listen: How Jude Bellingham became a global brand

Birmingham supporters have had little to cheer about recently.

It is 15 years since they last appeared in the Premier League, while the 2011 League Cup winners even dipped down to League One recently.

While fierce rivals Aston Villa were playing - and beating - Bayern Munich and Bologna in the Champions League two years ago, Birmingham were losing at Shrewsbury and drawing with Northampton Town.

After 15 games Birmingham sit top of the Championship and there are plans for a new 62,000-capacity stadium in time for 2030-31.

"As a club, we've been right down in the doldrums," added Courtney. "Now we're top of the table and having a new stadium built.

"There is an argument that none of this would have been possible without the fees received for Jude and Jobe."

A mural tribute to Jude Bellingham outside St Andrew's

Jude is the youngest player in Birmingham's history after making his debut aged 16 years and 38 days in 2019.

Clubs across Europe were pursuing him when he signed his first professional contact in 2020 after turning 17 - a deal both he and Birmingham knew would never be fulfilled.

His actions, however, ensured Birmingham would receive a significant transfer fee when he left, and soon afterwards he joined Dortmund for an initial fee of Â£20m during the Covid-19 pandemic.

When he joined Real in 2023, Birmingham received a reported sell-on fee of at least Â£10m., external

"We cannot possibly imagine, without Jude's decision [to sign a contract], where we would be as a club in a pandemic like this," then Birmingham chief executive Xuandong Ren told BBC WM after Jude joined Dortmund.

"He could easily have just looked after himself and not the club, but he chose the best possible way to look after the club."

Jobe became the second youngest player to play for Birmingham when he made his debut in January 2022 aged 16 years and 107 days.

"This was a lad, regardless of who his brother was or what he was achieving, who would do anything to write his own success story," former Birmingham striker Troy Deeney, who played in the game when Jobe made his debut, told the Sun., external

"Everything he has achieved on the pitch, too, has come with an instant comparison to his older brother.

"He never got that one moment to enjoy something without someone, somewhere saying: 'Yeah, but what about Jude?'

"That only added to how strong he was mentally, and anyone who suggests he is where he is because of his last name is talking rubbish."

Deeney added: "What impressed me more than anything he had done on the pitch was his attitude - a hell-bent determination to get to the top and the common sense to take all the right steps along the way."

Jobe played 26 games before Sunderland paid Â£3m for him in 2023, with Birmingham receiving a reported Â£4m sell-on fee when he moved to Dortmund two years later.

Although significantly less than the fees generated by his brother, it was nevertheless welcome revenue.

Jobe Bellingham was given his Birmingham City debut by manager Lee Bowyer in January 2022

Both Jude and Jobe have returned to St Andrew's since their transfers.

Jobe captained England Under-21s to a 2-0 win against the Republic of Ireland at his old ground last November.

Before that match U21s boss Lee Carsley, who managed Jude when he was England interim manager in 2024, praised the brothers for their work ethic and determination to be the best.

Carsley said: "I know how much they love the Blues still and how important the club is to them."

Jude, tipped to be a future England captain, was at St Andrew's in July watching his former club in a pre-season friendly against Barcelona. He even wore a Birmingham shirt while watching from the stands.

Jude wore a Birmingham City shirt when he returned to St Andrew's

When Jude joined Dortmund in 2020 Birmingham retired the 17-year-old's number 22 shirt after 44 appearances.

"That was a gesture of thanks for what Jude had done," said Courtney.

"It might be wishful thinking, but I really believe Jude has unfinished business at Birmingham. I can see a scenario before he retires where he gets an opportunity to wear the number 22 again."

Should the Bellingham brothers play together against Croatia, they will become the first siblings to appear for England since Gary and Phil Neville against Spain in a friendly at Old Trafford in 2007.

It will be an immensely proud moment for their parents, Mark and Denise.

"We've played together for so long in the street and to play with my brother Jobe for England would be the biggest dream of my life," Jude, a Champions League and La Liga winner with Real Madrid, wrote on social media, external in 2024.

"That would mean more than any of the trophies. Nothing would even get close to that... nothing."

BBC reporter John Watson has been finding out why Bellingham is proving so popular with football fans across the world

#913. Police investigation into Vigar's death ongoing

Billy Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025

The police investigation into the death of former Arsenal academy player Billy Vigar is ongoing, a coroner's court has heard.

Vigar died from a "significant brain injury" in September 2025, five days after colliding with a concrete wall surrounding a pitch while playing for Chichester City at Wingate and Finchley's stadium.

His parents, Keith and Camilla, told BBC Sport on the one-year anniversary that "the FA could have stopped Billy losing his life because they had so many warnings".

Acting Detective Sergeant Colin Chandler, from the Metropolitan Police, told a pre-inquest review hearing that he anticipated he would need another "two to three months" on his investigation.

He did not provide details on the lines of enquiry that the police are exploring.

BBC Sport has contacted the Met for comment.

Vigar's parents were present for the hearing at Barnet Coroner's Court on Thursday, as were representatives from the Football Association and Barnet Council.

Former Bath City player Alex Fletcher, who fractured his skull when colliding with concrete barriers next to the club's pitch in 2022, was also present, as was PFA representative Adam White.

Camilla Vigar told senior coroner Andrew Walker: "I don't understand how the FA waited for Billy to die before they actioned anything when there was so much warning beforehand.

"Ben Hiscox dying in 2015. Alex had his big accident in 2022. The investigation they did after that highlighted about 160 high-risk clubs. Wingate was one of them. They did nothing."

Keith Vigar spoke during the hearing to raise an "issue with Barnet not being an interested party" in the case.

"Personally I don't quite understand how the investigation carried out at the football club, Wingate and Finchley... I see it as a bit of a conflict of interest that Barnet as the local authority carried out that investigation. It feels like they are marking their own homework," he said.

A further hearing has been scheduled for 10 February.

Our son's death could have been prevented by FA - Billy Vigar's parents

#912. Kim Kardashian Reveals Status of Law Career After Failing Bar Exam

Kim Kardashian declared that she's "not giving up on trying to become a lawyer" over a year after failing the bar exam. The All’s Fair star has spent the last decade studying to be an attorney.

Yes, Kim Kardashian is keeping up with her lawyer aspirations.

The Kardashians star provided an update on whether she still intends on pursuing a career in law after failing the bar exam.

"I'm not giving up on trying to become a lawyer," Kardashian told Good Morning America on the red carpet at the All’s Fair season two premiere on Nov. 2. "I think that that was like a big misconception, but I do want to wait until the timing is right so that I know that I can do it without a ton of distractions around me."

"I don't know when that will be," she continued, "because there's always distractions. But it means a lot to me and I want to do it—and I'm gonna do it!"

The 46-year-old—who joked about failing the bar exam in an energy drink ad this past summer—had previously explained why she was so open about not getting the results she wanted on the test after completing a six-year law program.

"You get the results on a Friday, and I knew Sunday morning they were going to be live on the internet," she told the New York Times last December. "I was like, 'OK, let's do this, I know what I've got to do. This really sucks because I put so much time into it, but I know what I can do better.'"

The SKIMS founder continued, "I'm pretty good at taking a failure and turning it into something and I just don't have the time to dwell. You can feel sorry for yourself for a second, but I need to take that time and put it into studying more."

That said, she did have to take a short moment to privately process her results before making them public.

"I didn't feel good about it," Kardashian explained. "I was really uncomfortable and not confident for a while."

She's also always been clear about her intentions of following through with her lawyer aspirations. (Her late dad Robert Kardashian Sr. was an attorney.)

"Falling short isn't failure—it's fuel," she wrote on her Instagram Stories in Nov. 2025, after announcing her bar exam results. "I was so close to passing the exam and that only motivates me even more."

Kardashian's interest in becoming a lawyer is just one of the many career paths she's taken. Keep reading for more about her evolution over the years...

#911. Ghana kick-start Afcon 2027 bid despite Ayew penalty miss

Jordan Ayew joined Championship side Sheffield United in September after spending two seasons with Leicester City

Ghana belatedly kick-started their 2027 Africa Cup of Nations (Afcon) qualifying campaign with a 2-0 home win over Somalia.

The Black Stars had lost their opening two Group C matches against Ivory Coast and The Gambia, leading to the departure of coach Carlos Queiroz by mutual consent.

Ghana women's coach Kim Bjorkegren was placed in interim charge for this month's double-header against the Ocean Stars, with the West Africans in danger of missing a second successive edition of the Afcon finals.

The hosts were given a chance to take an early lead in Sekondi-Takoradi after Alidu Seidu was pulled down in the box, but Jordan Ayew's 14th-minute penalty was saved by Somalia goalkeeper Ibrahim Hussein.

Ghana did go ahead in first-half stoppage time when Mohammed Salisu headed Mohammed Kudus's deep corner back across goal and Jonas Adjetey nodded in from six yards out.

Felix Afena-Gyan doubled the Black Stars' advantage just after the hour mark when his shot from inside the box squirmed under Hussein and over the line.

The four-time continental champions remain six points behind group leaders Ivory Coast, who extended their 100% record by beating The Gambia 2-1 in Bouake.

Brighton midfielder Malick Yalcouye tucked in from seven yards out and Elye Wahi slotted home to double the Elephants' lead before Musa Barrow pulled one back for the visitors before the break.

Elsewhere on Thursday, there were wins for Cameroon, DR Congo and Senegal, who all remain on track to qualify for next year's tournament in Kenya, Tanzania and Uganda.

The third round of qualifying fixtures continues on Friday with Egypt, Morocco, Nigeria and South Africa in action among 12 fixtures.

Nicolas Jackson has 11 goals in 17 appearances for club and country this season

Nicolas Jackson set Senegal on their way to a 4-1 home win over Sudan in Group J, with Aston Villa team-mate Ibrahim Mbaye also on the scoresheet for Patrick Vieira's men in Dakar.

The Teranga Lions lead the standings on seven points, three ahead of Mozambique, who host Ethiopia on Friday.

Cameroon also remained unbeaten and moved on to seven points in Group G with a comfortable 2-0 victory over Namibia in Douala.

Meanwhile, Newcastle United striker Yoane Wissa opened the scoring as DR Congo continued their perfect start with a 3-1 triumph over Sierra Leone in Kinshasa.

The Leopards are on nine points at the top of Group E, five points ahead of Zimbabwe and Equatorial Guinea after those two sides drew 0-0.

Nigeria were handed a boost after Group L leaders Guinea-Bissau could only manage a 1-1 draw in their away tie against Madagascar in neutral Morocco.

The Super Eagles trail Guinea-Bissau by four points ahead of their home game against Tanzania on Friday (16:00 GMT).

Tanzania are assured of a place at Afcon 2027 as tournament co-hosts, with the other three sides battling for one qualification spot.

And Benin bolstered their bid to reach back-to-back finals with a 4-1 win over Central African Republic.

Gernot Rohr's Cheetahs lead Group F by three points from Burkina Faso, who entertain Mauritania on Friday.

In Group D, another section with just one spot available, Guinea moved level on points with table-toppers South Africa after seeing off Eritrea 2-1 in Conakry.

#910. Christian Cousins, Kindergarten Cop Actor, Dead at 43

Christian Cousins, a former child actor who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop, died at 43 in October, his brother shared.

Christian Cousins—who starred alongside Arnold Schwarzenegger in Kindergarten Cop in the ‘90s—died in October, his brother Jonas Roeser confirmed on social media. He was 43.

“It’s hard to share that my brother, Christian Cousins, has passed away,” Jonas captioned an Oct. 22 Instagram post, within which he noted that he connected with Christian and his twin brother Joseph Cousins later in life. “They grew up in California while I was in Washington and I didn’t get to know them until I was in college. Before that, I grew up watching them on television in Knots Landing and the lead role of Dominic in Kindergarten Cop with Arnold Schwarzenegger.”

“But those roles are only a small part of how I’ll remember Christian,” Jonas continued. “He was a character, full of passion and energy, with big stories and even bigger dreams.”

He noted that Christian had been battling liver disease, though he did not share additional information.

“It brings me comfort to believe he is now in heaven with his mother, free from the pain he was carrying,” Jonas concluded. “Rest easy, Christian. I hope your soul is at rest and that you’ve found peace. You are my brother and you will be missed.”

Christian and his twin Joseph shared the role of Dominic in the 1990 film Kindergarten Cop, which saw Arnold play LAPD detective John Kimble, who is forced to go undercover as a kindergarten teacher.

In addition to the beloved film, Christian appeared in the series Knot’s Landing as Bobby Gibson Ewing, again sharing the role with Joseph, and had credits on 1991’s Critters 3, 1992’s Intruders and Twin Sitters in 1994.

He pivoted away from acting, however, and in 2020­—during a virtual reunion with Arnold and the cast of Kindergarten Cop—revealed an executive for a furniture business and co-owned a CBD company.

During the conversation, Arnold expressed his disbelief to see the cast of the series so grown up, noting, “It is the funniest thing to see all of you guys.”

Christian, for his part, had some thank yous to extend to the Terminator actor, courtesy of his character Dominic.

“By the way, after 30 years I want to thank you again for saving my life from Richard Tyson in the locker room,” Christian said in reference to the film, adding of the fact Detective Kimble ends up with his onscreen mother, “And I’m glad you ended up with my mom for that movie. That was awesome.”

#909. Massive atlas of brain region linked to a host of diseases is the most detailed yet

Thank you for visiting nature.com. You are using a browser version with limited support for CSS. To obtain the best experience, we recommend you use a more up to date browser (or turn off compatibility mode in Internet Explorer). In the meantime, to ensure continued support, we are displaying the site without styles and JavaScript.

Miryam Naddaf is a reporter for Nature in London.

An MRI scan of the basal ganglia, seen here in section and colour-coded.Credit: Zephyr/SPL

The basal ganglia are groups of cells that sit deep in the brain and process motor, cognitive, mood and decision-making information. They are linked to neurodegenerative and psychiatric conditions from Parkinson’s and Huntington’s disease to schizophrenia, bipolar disorder and addiction.

Now, researchers have published the world’s most-detailed atlas of basal ganglia so far, comprising 25.5 million brain cells from humans, macaques and marmosets. The work is described in a collection of 26 papers published in Cell, Cell Reports, Cell Reports Methods, Cell Systems, Cell Genomics and Neuron. The research includes understudied neurons1, provides insights about how some brain cells change with age2 and suggests which might be linked to diseases3.

The atlas, a collaboration between hundreds of scientists in nine countries, is part of the BRAIN Initiative Cell Atlas Network (BICAN) — a US$500-million project launched in 2022 by the US National Institutes of Health aimed at creating reference maps of mammalian brains.

“It’s a massive dictionary that we needed in the field,” says Ana Muñoz-Manchado, a neuroscientist at the University of Cádiz in Spain, who studies the basal ganglia in neurodegenerative disorders.

The basal ganglia atlas contains 21 million cells from the brains of six humans, three million cells from three rhesus and cynomolgus macaques, and 1.5 million cells from two marmosets4. The researchers also used data from previously published maps of the whole mouse brain5,6.

By comparing the basal ganglia between the primate species, the researchers identified 61 cell types in humans, macaques and marmosets that have been conserved over 76 million years3.

The team analysed brain tissue samples from different developmental stages across the lifespan of the species. The latest work combines information about these cells in unprecedented detail, from measurements of their gene expression and DNA modifications that control gene regulation to recordings of their electrical activity, as well as how DNA is folded inside their nuclei.

The researchers also mapped where each cell is located in the brain and designed a common framework to characterize and annotate the cells. It is “essentially a scaffold on which we can now fairly readily complete the rest of the brain”, explains Michael Hawrylycz, a bioinformatician at the Allen Institute for Brain Science in Seattle, Washington, who took part in the project.

One study examined 1.1 million cells in the basal ganglia’s largest structure — known as the striatum — from 19 deceased human donors7. Unlike many other brain areas, the striatum has no neat anatomical boundaries. The researchers identified six zones in the human and macaque striatum that had distinct molecular signatures, each containing distinct populations of neurons and glial cells.

“The cells in these zones all look the same under the microscope, but have very strong transcriptional differences and are strikingly consistent from person to person,” said co-author Evan Macosko, a neurobiologist at the Broad Institute of Harvard and MIT in Cambridge, Massachusetts, in a press release from the institute.

Macosko and his colleagues also found that gene expression patterns that distinguished each zone from the other became increasingly similar with age, particularly in brain regions affected by Huntington’s or Parkinson’s disease.

Another study analysed nearly four million cells in the striatum and prefrontal cortex from 178 deceased adult donors aged from 27 to more than 902. The researchers found that the cellular make-up of the two brain regions varied between people, particularly for non-neuronal cells known as glial cells. This underscores the need for brain cell atlases to account for these individual differences.

#908. SFA in talks with Boston officials over biennial friendly match

The Tartan Army made a big impression on the city of Boston during the World Cup

BBC Scotland has learned that the SFA is in active discussions aimed at a biennial friendly match being held in Boston.

Scotland played two World Cup matches in the US city during the summer and now the governing body and the state of Massachusetts are in talks aimed at building the bonds made between locals and the Tartan Army, through football.

More discussions are due to take place between the SFA and a delegation of state senators ahead of Scotland's Nations League match against North Macedonia at Hampden on Friday.

It has not yet been decided who will play in the game but BBC Scotland understands it will involve the Scoland national team.

US state senator Paul Feeney has been in the UK this week for talks around energy, but wanted to visit Scotland to build on the bonds made between the Tartan Army and those who partied with them for two weeks in June.

The state of Massachusetts has also passed a bill aimed at strengthening ties with Scotland after an estimated 25,000 fans partied in Boston and surrounding areas.

"We felt that this summer was more than just a football match, more than just, you know, 90 minutes at Gillette Stadium in Foxborough," Feeney said.

"It was a couple of weeks of these relationships being held, and you don't see that often. And I'm glad we got to experience it. And, frankly, we don't want that to end."

He added: "One of the things that we've been active on in Massachusetts today is to kind of take the lessons that we've learned, put together the best practices, and say, ok, we understand that we can't have a World Cup every year, but where we have such a strong connection with people in Scotland, could we do some sort of invitational tournament?

"To have that cultural exchange to kind of prop up economic development, and more than that, just to come together, have a few drinks, and enjoy each other's company."

Scotland fans placed cones on several Boston statues during their time in the city

Feeney said the Massachusetts Senate voted unanimously to support the concept.

"We're trying to work that through the legislature, get it to the finish," he said.

Talks aimed at organising a regular fixture are at an early stage but the SFA is already in advanced negotiations with businesses in Massachusetts about investment in the Scottish game.

"The Tartan Army invaded Massachusetts and I have to say they lit a spark that set off fireworks," Massachusetts Senate president Karen Spilka told BBC Scotland.

"They were sorely missed by so many people when they left.

"I think that by making the effort to come here and meet people and talk about tourism and economic development, we can start talking about things like Tartan Day and maybe having other events going on."

#907. Less drama, more listening, but is Kozo Tashima the candidate to topple Infantino?

Japan FA honorary president is hoping a calmer approach that makes fewer unwelcome headlines for Fifa will be welcomed by football

Not many remember Japan’s bid for the 2022 World Cup, when the country finished the race with only two of the final 22 votes. Kozo Tashima was involved then, and now the honorary president of the Japan Football Association is going it alone in the hope of ousting Gianni Infantino.

The 68-year-old Tashima is an unlikely insurgent and an unlikely challenger to Infantino. He is, however, a familiar and respected figure in Asian and global football politics, and ready to take the Fifa presidency out of the headlines into a quieter era.

In 2010, during the JFA’s failed World Cup bid, Tashima proved himself to be an affable campaigner, impressing with his efficiency and, in the words of an official from one European association, displaying a rare ability for a football leader to listen more than talk. He may not have the ability for an easy quip, or as much charm and charisma as Infantino or his predecessor, Sepp Blatter, but that could count in his favour.

Since entering the Fifa Council in 2015, Tashima has rarely made an international headline and it is this, he hopes, that will make a difference. Tashima is ready to put principles to the fore before March’s election. “It’s not about winning or losing but about conveying to the world the honest, sound and upright attitude that Japanese football has built,” Tashima said as he announced his candidacy for the Fifa presidency on 5 November. “What Fifa needs now are these values that we have protected. I have decided to run in order to make this appeal to the world.”

Tashima became the JFA’s technical director in 2002, moving up to the role of federation president as Japan became Asia’s leading football nation. Off the pitch, however, the power has moved westwards, from Tokyo to Riyadh, Doha and Manama. There has been disquiet about how the Asian Football Confederation has, from Japan’s perspective, become too close to Saudi Arabia and Qatar.

The feeling about Fifa is worse. JFA officials were dismayed at Infantino’s closeness to Donald Trump. Given how crucial a partner the United States has been to Japan in terms of security and as an export market for more than eight decades, the president’s actions in regards to tariffs and cosying up to China and North Korea went down badly in Tokyo, as did Trump’s favourability, going below 30% in May.

The summer was the last straw, with the Folarin Balogun affair during the World Cup and then the leaking of Infantino’s plan to sell off the tournament’s commercial rights to private investors. Yet in October the JFA president, Tsuneyasu Miyamoto, the former defender who succeeded Tashima in 2024, followed the AFC leadership and backed Infantino. Miyamoto’s decision resulted in the resignation of the JFA vice-president, Takeshi Okada.

“I have always believed that sports should be noble and have cherished their social value,” said Okada, a former Japan defender and national team head coach. “However, the recent actions surrounding the Fifa World Cup have created a significant gap between my beliefs and the actions taken, and as a sportsman I could not accept them, which led me to this decision.”

Okada led Japan at the 2010 World Cup in South Africa but only after surviving calls from fans and the media for him to be sacked due to poor results in preparation for the tournament. Tashima’s support as JFA president was key to this and his loyalty was rewarded with seeing the Samurai Blue reach the knockout stages on foreign soil for a first time. Now it was Okada’s turn to back Tashima and he did just that as the latter announced his candidacy for the Fifa presidency, one that came as a surprise to most in Asia.

There is an expectation that Uefa’s candidate will be announced soon, but if no one is put up by Europe’s governing body then Tashima becomes the main challenger to Infantino’s supremacy, ahead of the former Tottenham defender Ramon Vega, who has also announced his candidacy. He would automatically get some support from Europe and Concacaf members but may not have the international connections to pick up enough votes elsewhere.

Tashima, who earned seven caps for Japan in the late 1970s and early 1980s, is not going to unite Asia, but there will also be backing for him from the east and south-east, where the JFA has worked hard over the years building relationships with national associations such as those of Singapore and Thailand. Tashima has put his chances of winning at between 20% and 30% but, as he said, this isn’t really about winning but about standing up for what is right.

If Tashima does win, there will be a Fifa president who looks to build consensus behind the scenes and make as few headlines as possible. There will also be no cosying up to world leaders, or certainly not any more than is absolutely necessary. Football fans may well appreciate a quieter, less visible, less controversial man at the top of the sport’s world governing body. Kozo Tashima could be that man.

#906. Choi pushing for first LPGA win at The Annika as Korda drops back

Hye-Jin Choi shares the lead with Carlota Ciganda and Lindy Duncan as she chases a first LPGA victory; Nelly Korda was four shots back at the end of the second day; Watch round three of The Annika on LPGA Tour from 7pm on Saturday, live on Sky Sports Mix

Hye-Jin Choi opened with two bogeys, made up ground with a 15-foot eagle putt late and finished with a three-under 67 on Friday that gave her part of a three-way share of the lead at The Annika.

It was far more effective than the bogey-free round of Nelly Korda, the No. 1 player who could only laugh at her clean card because it was cleaner than she would have preferred - 15 straight pars, one birdie, two closing pars for a 69.

That left Korda four shots behind going into the weekend at Pelican Golf Club, where a victory would make the 28-year-old American eligible for the LPGA Hall of Fame.

"I had a lot of chances," said Korda, competing for the first time in two months. "But you can just tell that from yesterday morning to today afternoon with the wind, that's what the defence of this golf course is. It's as fast as Bermuda as I've putted on throughout my career."

It wasn't a problem for Solheim Cup star Carlota Ciganda, who birdied her last four holes for a 63 to join Choi and Lindy Duncan (66) atop the leaderboard at 12-under 128.

The Japanese duo of Mao Saigo (65) and Minami Katsu (69) were two shots behind.

Choi has been an LPGA member for five years and it has been a curious chase for that first LPGA victory, particularly since she was 17 when she had a late lead in the 2017 US Women's Open and wound up as a runner-up.

She also had two good chances at winning during the recent Asia swing, where she was runner-up in Shanghai and South Korea.

Choi was playing in the group with Korda for the opening two rounds, which she believes has tested her enough to calm her nerves on the weekend. She wasn't rattled by the bogey-bogey start, or the bogey on the par-five 14th, her fifth hole of the round.

She pieced together enough birdies to regain some momentum, then hit an approach that got a nice kick around the green and rolled out to just under 15 feet for eagle on the par-five seventh.

"I have two rounds left, but I have recently played in a champion group on the tournament before, so I have that experience and I'm going just try my best and concentrate on my game," Choi said.

Scoring was low enough in the opening round that one-under 139 made the cut. This is the final regular-season event of the year, and the top 60 in the Race to CME Globe advance to the finale next week in Naples, where the winner gets $2 million.

Julia Lopez Ramirez of Spain, who defeated Yealimi Noh in a crucial singles match in her Solheim Cup debut, was among those at nine-under 131. That was important for the Spaniard, who came into the week at No. 66 in the Race to the CME Globe.

Duncan, the 35-year-old Floridian, has yet to win on the LPGA Tour and this was the first time she had at least a share of the lead through 36 holes. She went 2-1 in her Solheim Cup debut.

"The week has gone by really fast, which is sometimes a good thing," Duncan said. "Because if you're playing a lot and you get some momentum going, that's kind of a nice way to play. So it's just been kind of rolling with it."

Charley Hull was five shots off the leaders on seven-under after shooting 67 on Friday. England's Lottie Woad finished the second round level with Hull on seven-under.

Avril Lavigne shared she has welcomed her first child, giving a glimpse at her and her unnamed partner's baby girl: “Our mini f--king princess has arrived.”

The "Sk8er Boi" musician recently shared a major glimpse into her private world, confirming she is now a mom after welcoming her first child, a baby girl.

"Our mini f--king princess," she captioned a Nov. 13 Instagram post featuring photos of her holding her daughter, three pairs of vans as well as her hand and another holding their baby's finger, "has arrived.”

Prior to expanding her family, over the years, Lavigne, 42—who hasn't shared details about the identity of her baby's father—has kept her personal life close to the vest.

She was married to Sum 41 alum Deryck Whibley for three years until 2009, ending their relationship on amicable terms.

"Deryck and I have been together for 6-and-a-half years,” she wrote on her website at the time. “We have been friends since I was 17, started dating when I was 19, and married when I was 21. I am grateful for our time together, and I am grateful and blessed for our remaining friendship."

In fact, their breakup just wasn’t complicated.

"I admire Deryck and have a great amount of respect for him,” she continued. “He is the most amazing person I know and I love him with all my heart. Deryck and I are separating and moving forward on a positive note.”

And when she met second husband Chad Kroeger in 2012, she ultimately decided that she wanted to be more than just his girlfriend, with the couple exchanging vows just a year later. However, by 2015, her relationship with the Nickelback singer met a different ending.

"It is with [a] heavy heart that Chad and I announce our separation today,” she wrote on social media at the time. “Through not only the marriage, but the music as well, we've created many unforgettable moments. We are still, and forever will be, the best of friends, and will always care deeply for each other. To all our family, friends and fans, thank you sincerely for the support."

Since then, Lavigne has been linked to Brody Jenner, Mod Sun and most recently in 2023, Tyga. And though she’s rarely shared insight into her personal life, the “Complicated” singer has opened up about taking a step back from the spotlight entirely.

"I spent the last few years at home sick fighting Lyme Disease,” she wrote on her personal website in 2018. “Those were the worst years of my life as I went through both physical and emotional battles. I was able to turn that fight into music I'm really proud of. I wrote songs in my bed and on the couch and recorded there mostly as well. Words and lyrics that were so true to my experience came pouring out of me effortlessly. Truly... by keeping my spirits up, having goals to reach and a purpose to live for, my music helped to heal me and keep me alive."

"I'm taking my life back into my own hands and doing what it is I know I am meant to be doing in this life time,” she added. “Making music.”

#902. Nations League: Italy roar back to beat France despite Donnarumma’s early howler

Loss is Zinedine Zidane’s first as France head coach

Spain beat Czechia 2-0 to maintain 100% record

Pio Esposito struck twice to inflict a first defeat on Zinedine Zidane as France head coach as Italy stormed back to win 3-1 at San Siro and go top of their Nations League group.

Michael Olise profited on a Gianluigi Donnarumma error to put the visitors in front after 10 minutes, but Italy hit back through Esposito and Davide Frattesi either side of half-time.

Inter striker Esposito’s second came from the penalty spot after his brother Sebastiano had earlier fired a spot-kick wide, while France were twice denied by the woodwork in an entertaining encounter.

The result sent Italy top of Group A1 on 10 points, level with France but above them on head-to-head record, while Belgium are third on nine points after inflicting a fifth straight defeat on rock-bottom Turkey.

France were without Kylian Mbappé and Ousmane Dembélé through injury, but it did not show as they made an electric start under pouring rain in Milan. Désiré Doué hit the side netting and first-time captain Adrien Rabiot tested Donnarumma before Lucas Da Cunha’s rasping half-volley flew narrowly wide.

However, the opener was gifted to France when Donnarumma passed the ball straight to Olise, who skipped past a defender before firing home his fifth goal in five Nations League games – a record only bettered by England captain Harry Kane’s seven.

The hosts struck back in the 26th minute with their first chance of the game when Nicolò Cambiaghi drove to the byline and cut back a cross, which Esposito converted with a deft touch. The goal brought San Siro to life as the older Esposito sibling, Sebastiano, threatened a quickfire comeback two minutes later when he forced a sharp save from Mike Maignan.

Bradley Barcola came closest to a third goal before the break with a curling shot from the edge of the box that struck the foot of the far post.

The end-to-end nature of the game continued in the second half as Rayan Cherki’s rasping strike was tipped on to a post by Donnarumma before Italy charged up the other end and forced Maignan into a point-blank save from Cambiaghi. Italy had a glorious chance to go in front when Cambiaghi was tripped by Malo Gusto to earn a penalty, but Sebastiano Esposito failed to join his brother on the scoresheet as he hammered his spot-kick wide on the hour mark.

The Azzurri did not dwell on the disappointment for long, taking the lead just three minutes later when Frattesi drilled in a shot from a Federico Dimarco cross moments after the Inter wing-back was brought off the bench. Fellow substitute Antonio Vergara earned the home side another penalty when he was tripped by Dayot Upamecano, and this time Pio Esposito stepped up to drill a shot into the bottom corner.

The result continued a strong start to Roberto Mancini’s second spell as Italy coach as his side stretched their unbeaten run to four matches and notched their first home win over France since 1962.

Belgium are third after Kevin De Bruyne scored in their 2-1 triumph in Turkey.

During a goal-frenzied first half at Gursel Aksel Stadium, Arda Güler put Turkey ahead with a stunning free-kick from 25 yards out before De Bruyne levelled seven minutes after a cutback from Jérémy Doku. Charles De Ketelaere fired in after Diego Moreira’s shot was saved to earn Belgium all three points.

Belgium host Italy and Turkey travel to France in the final round of group games on Sunday.

Álex Baena scored from the spot and Marc Pubill added another seconds from time as Spain beat 10-man Czechia 2-0 in Group A3. The win in Prague leaves Spain unbeaten for 44 competitive games, including five wins in as many Nations League games this season.

Kick off your evenings with the Guardian's take on the world of football

Spain, who already secured a quarter-final berth before travelling to Prague, will face England in Madrid on Sunday in their final Group A3 game.

Baena scored on 39 minutes after a VAR check revealed Czechia midfielder Lukas Ambros had handled the ball inside the box. The Atlético Madrid winger blasted his spot-kick past Matej Kovar who touched the ball but failed to clear it.

Home captain Ladislav Krejci was sent off in the 69th minute after bringing down second-half substitute Roberto Fernández on a counterattack. Pubill, another substitute, beat Kovar with a low shot deep into stoppage time after the Czechia back four left him alone facing the Eindhoven goalkeeper.

Luis de la Fuente missed Lamine Yamal, Dani Olmo, Rodri and Eric García with injuries while Mikel Oyarzabal was sidelined with flu.

Fabián Ruiz hit a post with a curling right-footer three minutes from half-time, while Dean Huijsen’s header found Kovar’s arms.

Yéremy Pino, replacing Yamal on the right flank, saw his goal overturned by VAR for offside just two minutes into the second half.

Czechia showed higher spirits after the break, but David Zima put an effort over on 50 minutes and Adam Hlozek’s glancing header landed on the top of the crossbar.

The hosts lost momentum after the red card, but Baena had two efforts cleared by Kovar who also denied Fernández from close range.

The hosts, led by De la Fuente’s long-time collaborator Santi Denia, have lost all their Nations League games this season. They are next travelling to Croatia for a game they need to win to stay in the top tier of the competititon for the next edition.

#901. High Potential Reveals Season 3 Premiere Date on ABC

High Potential season three will premiere midseason on ABC, with the Kaitlin Olson series set to return in early 2027, nine months after its cliffhanger season two finale in April 2026.

Morgan Gillory will be back to solving crimes very soon.

High Potential's third season will premiere Jan. 5, 2027, on ABC, the network confirmed after previously announcing that it wouldn't be part of its fall 2026 slate as expected.

"Hi, I'm Morgan," the show's star Kaitlin Olson said in a video posted to the show's official Instagram Nov. 7. "I'm a consultant for the LAPD, and I tend to see things that other people miss."

"For example, bet you didn't see this," she added before the clip revealed its season three premiere date. "I'm a genius, don't feel bad—unless you're also a genius and then, maybe you should."

Naturally, fans of High Potential—which concluded its second season back in April—celebrated the news in the comment section, with one person writing, "I feel like I've just been reborn."

A second person commented that they "missed her sarcasm so much," while another user said that they "literally cannot wait" for the show's return.

Season three will give fans answers after season two ended with a shocking finale cliffhanger, with Steve Howey's Captain Nick Wagner's fate up in the air after Mallory found him with stab wounds.

Olson—who is also an executive producer on the series—admitted after the episode aired that it featured "a lot of cliffhangers" and that Nick "was stabbed a lot."

"There are so many places that we can go with this next season," she told People in May. "It's very exciting and it definitely starts with, does Wagner make it or not?"

Regardless of whether or not Nick survives his injuries, his dog Ingrid will be just fine.

"Oh my God! Don't even worry about the dog," Olson shared. "Ingrid's coming home. The entire season can be about that dog as far as I'm concerned. I loved her."

#900. BBC to show Dover v Leicester and Salisbury v Blackpool

Leicester City will travel to Crabble, the home of Dover Athletic of National League South

Non-league clubs Dover Athletic and Salisbury will stage the BBC's two chosen FA Cup second-round ties next month.

National League South side Dover welcome former Premier League and FA Cup winners Leicester City to Crabble on Saturday, 5 December (17:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Another sixth-tier side, Salisbury, will host Blackpool, winners of one of the most memorable finals of all time in 1953, at the Raymond McEnhill Stadium the following day (Sunday 6 December, 12:15 GMT, BBC Two/iPlayer).

Dover reached the second round courtesy of a 2-0 home win over National League side Wealdstone and are seeking to reach round three for just the third time in their history, having lost against Huddersfield in 2011 and at home to Premier League outfit Crystal Palace in 2015.

The Foxes - who lost on their first four FA Cup final appearances before Youri Tielemans' goal secured a 1-0 win over Chelsea in the 2021 final - now play in League One after back-to-back relegations and overcame Oxford City of National League North 4-2 in the first round.

Salisbury are yet to concede a goal in their three ties this season and thrashed Sholing 6-0 to reach round two for the first time since the club was reformed in 2015.

Seventh-tier sides Wimborne Town and Plymouth Parkway will also see their home ties against League One Bradford City and League Two Barnet, respectively, televised among the eight selected for live coverage across the weekend.

All clubs featured in live television broadcasts will receive Â£60,000 while the winning and losing clubs in the second round will receive Â£79,500 and Â£21,200 respectively from the competition prize fund.

The third round draw will take place before the televised tie between Guiseley and Notts County at 19:30 GMT on Monday, 7 December.

A comprehensive highlights programme will cover the weekend's action on Sunday, 6 December at 17:10 GMT (BBC Two/iPlayer).

All of the second round's goals will be available to view across BBC digital platforms including the BBC Sport website and app.

#899. Who Is Sam Hartman? What to Know About the New Bachelor Lead

The Bachelor just announced that NFL quarterback Sam Hartman will lead the ABC dating franchise’s 30th season, set to air in March 2027. See everything to know about the athlete.

The Bachelor just announced that its upcoming 30th season will have a major twist—tapping Washington Commanders quarterback Sam Hartman as the leading man for the ABC reality dating show.

“I’m excited but I’m also so nervous,” Hartman said on Good Morning America Nov. 13. “I have a tough time holding conversation with one girl. 30 is going to be pretty tough.”

Nevertheless, Hartman’s huddle couldn’t be more thrilled that he’s passing out petals instead of throwing passes.

“They’re excited,” the 27-year-old revealed of his family’s reaction to the news. “My mom and I have a really cool relationship, and my pops is obviously just supportive. And their big thing is just be myself and enjoy the experience, and you know, trust the instincts and trust your gut.”

Hartman’s casting marks the first time in years the franchise's Bachelor wasn’t picked from the pool of prior Bachelorette contestants—but that’s not the only unique quality Hartman is bringing to the Fantasy Suite.

Below, find a play-by-play of all the X’s and O’s to know about Hartman.

After playing college football at the University of Notre Dame, Hartman was drafted into the United Football League in 2024, playing for the Birmingham Stallions. That same year, he signed with the Washington Commanders as an undrafted free agent.

Hartman has remained a member of the Commanders’ practice squad and acts as their backup quarterback. He has yet to play in a regular season NFL game.

Yes, Hartman is still an active player for the Commanders, although he has not yet made his NFL debut.

After his casting in The Bachelor was announced, Hartman shared that his teammates were throwing support his way—but joked he might not catch all of it.

“My teammates were giving me some advice on the plane ride back,” he explained on Good Morning America. “So, probably not going to listen to anybody on that. But no, I'm excited.”

While Hartman will be flown around the country come hometowns, he calls Charlotte, North Carolina home.

He attended SouthLake Christian Academy in Huntersville and played three seasons of football at Davidson Day School before attending Wake Forest University prior to his transfer to Notre Dame, according to WBTV.

After being announced at the next Bachelor, Hartman admitted he’s made more than a few fumbles when it comes to his dating life. The athlete said that charming 30 women on the upcoming season, set to air in March 2027, will be “tough.”

Similarly, Hartman’s social media profiles appear to be strictly business—as most of his posts are dedicated to football.

No, Hartman is not the first football player to hand out roses. In fact, host and NFL alum Jesse Palmer—who has acted as franchise host since 2021—was a contestant himself during season five after playing in the NFL for five seasons.

Meanwhile, Golden Bachelor alum Mel Owens previously played for the Los Angeles Rams, while Colton Underwood similarly spent time with the Philadelphia Eagles, Las Vegas Raiders and the Los Angeles Chargers, although he never played in a regular season NFL game.

The Bachelor season 26 star Clayton Echard also spent time with the Seattle Seahawks in 2016 for training camp.

Initially, Hartman admitted he told ABC “no way” to the proposition of becoming The Bachelor franchise’s next leading man.

“The connotation of it, I was like, ‘I don’t know,’” Hartman explained on Good Morning America. “Then, I got really lucky and talked to Jesse Palmer. He kind of gave me the insight and gave me the, what it is and what it’s not.”

Ultimately, Hartman is willing to throw a spiral into the dark if it means meeting his soulmate.

“Anybody in their right mind if you get told, ‘Hey you’ve got a chance to go find the love of your life,’” Hartman continued. “I know one thing, when people are saying ‘I do’ they don’t ask you where you met, they just ask you if you want to do it forever and I don’t see any problem with that.”

Nevertheless, the quarterback admitted he was “very nervous.”

To revisit all the past Bachelor Nation-made pairs and where they are now, keep reading…

Even before Mel Owen's season of The Golden Bachelor kicked off, he was hit with a few penalties after going on the MGoBlue Podcasts With Jon Jansen and insisting, "if they’re 60 or over, I’m cutting them," adding that he wanted them to "try to stay away from the artificial hips and the wigs."

And while Peg Munson is a fellow sexagenarian, his connection with the retired firefighter and bomb tech was quite explosive, with the former NFL linebacker praising her as "high-energy" to Glamour.

Though he didn't take a knee during his November 2025 finale, the sports lawyer still offered up a Neil Lane sparkler, saying, "This represents our commitment to love, to give us time to figure out together what our future holds."

Munson announced in October 2026 that the couple had split, sharing on Instagram, "I did have to make the difficult decision to step away from the relationship. Sometimes, even when there's love, it just doesn't turn out the way that we hoped. So right now, I'm just, I'm just focusing on healing my heart and just focusing on myself, my health, and looking forward to the next chapter.”

According to Spencer Conley (who intrigued Jenn Tran with his "golden retriever energy" on The Bachelorette), he fetched quite the catch on the 10th season of Bachelor in Paradise. Posting a snippet of himself and Jess Edwards (she took a swing at Bachelor Joey Graziadei's heart) revealing that they were falling for one another—Bachelor code for I'm not quite ready to say, "I love you"—he wrote on his Instagram Stories in August 2025 that he'd "already won."

Hard same from Jess, who wrote on her main feed, "just feeling a lil giddy about this man & whatnot."

And they were certainly smiling when, after choosing their relationship over the $250,000 prize, they got engaged and walked away with a surprise check worth $190,000.

"Everything that we’ve been through," Jess said, "has led us to this exact moment."

Since then, their love led her to Dallas, Jess revealing during Mel's November 2025 After the Finale Rose special that she was Texas-bound in a few weeks.

"This was my best first date," Bailey Taylor Brown wrote on Instagram in August 2025 after she took Jeremy Simon out on Paradise's 10th season. And perhaps her last? The social media manger, who initially competed for Grant Ellis' heart, and the real estate investor who nearly charmed Bachelorette Jenn managed to survive their most dramatic squabble ever when she learned he had second thoughts about sending Susie Evans home.

Still, their connection continued to heat up in Costa Rica. And while they were sent home during the Bachelor in Paradise finale, they continued to pursue a relationship off-camera. In fact, the show revealed that they've met each other families and that they're planning to move to the same city.

"We feel so lucky to have found each other," Bailey wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and couldn’t be more excited for what’s to come."

Seems the connection between Paradise season 10 pair Andrew Spencer (one of Katie Thurston's suitors) and Alexe Godin (from Grant's season) has remained trés strong post-show. Six days after the Chicago-based football player dubbed the pedatric speech therapist "mon amour" in an August 2025 Instagram post, she labeled him "mon chéri" in her own missive.

And while they chose love over the $250,000 prize during the BiP finale, they still got to head home with $125,000 in their pockets.

"This is frickin unreal," Alexe said. "I am leaving with money, but not just money—love, the most important thing."

And they're bringing their love to the Windy City, with the show revealing Alexe's plans to move to Chicago with Andrew.

"Finally found someone just as weird as me," she wrote on Instagram in September 2025, "and I can’t wait to do life with you."

Kat Izzo and Dale Moss went through a thorny moment during the Bachelor in Paradise finale when former contestant Sean McLaughlin alleged she "stashed a laptop" and had been sending an ex love letters. However, the nurse practitioner denied contacting him on the show.

"Did me and my ex still have a relationship prior to this?" she said. "Yes, because I didn’t think I was gonna meet anybody here."

While Kat and Dale were sent home before the final test of Paradise, their romance continued to bloom. The show revealed the alum from Zach Shallcross' season and the former contestant from Clare Crawley's went on to travel across the U.S. together and made plans to build a future together, including moving closer.

"It was tough at times," Dale commented under Kat's August 2025 Instagram post, "but we navigated it together…and I wouldn’t change a thing."

But their journey came to a close in early 2026.

Among the issues Kat detailed during a January appearance on the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast was his unwillingness to relocate from NYC.

"San Diego is apparently, to him, not anywhere he could grow his career," she explained. "I never really got full answers. I don’t really know what the true reason was."

Golden Bachelorette alum Gary Levingston and Leslie Fhima (a runner up for Golden Bachelor Gerry Turner's heart) appeared to have quite the glittery future when they were voted off Bachelor in Paradise's 10th season, even writing about "making new memories" in a post-elimination social media video. But the onetime Prince muse isn't quite sure if she wants to be his lover.

"We talk all the time," she revealed during an August 2025 appearance on Bachelor Happy Hour. "Gary is, I can honestly say right now, one of my best friends. I’ll call him if I have a problem. He kind of talks me off the ledge a little bit, and we are always there for each other. We have each other’s back."

While she acknowledged that the nearly 2,000 miles between them (she's based in Minnesota; he's in California) complicates the situation, she hasn't given up hope. "All I know is that for me, a big thing with any relationship, a romantic one for sure, is I want to be friends first," she continued. "Because I want to be with my best friend growing older."

Golden Bachelorette's head mansion man Kim Buike found someone to make sweet music with in Gerry Turner's first impression rose recipient Faith Martin. Though they were eliminated on the 10th season of Paradise, they sailed off into the sunset, with Faith posting a video to Instagram in August 2025 of the retired navy captain enjoying a hometown date with her in Washington.

However, they ultimately realized they weren't each other's person and that they were better off as friends.

"We talk sometimes two to three times a week," Faith said in a September 2025 Instagram video. "He lives five and a half hours away. But the point is this: We are not a in-love couple. Nope, we are not. We never fell in love. We had a great connection on the show."

Status: SplitGrant may have met 25 potential love interests on his first night in the Bachelor mansion, but in the end, it was Juliana Pasquarosa who scored his final rose. However, the couple decided to call it quits less than three months after their propsal aired.

Drama continued to play out when Devin shared a 13-minute video recounting his side of the story to Instagram, where in addition to taking "accountability” he shared insight into why he ended the relationship in a 15-minute phone call.

There, the two announced that they were in a relationship. In April 2024, he revealed the two had called it quits.

Status: SplitBefore Victoria Fuller and Greg Grippo went public with their romance on the finale of Bachelor in Paradise's eighth season, she and her costar Johnny DePhillipo ended their engagement.

"While our paths are taking different directions due to our career goals not aligning," they wrote in a joint Instagram post, "we are grateful for the love and support we’ve received from our family, friends, and Bachelor Nation."

Status: SplitDespite her nerves about a Paradise engagement, an all-dressed-in-white Eliza Isichei (one of Clayton Echard's exes) happily accepted Aaron Bryant's oceanfront proposal. Touched by the software salesman's decision to reach out to her mom for her blessing, she gushed, "I knew I was not in control of what was going to come out of my mouth." The finale's coda acknowledged Charity's ex and marketing manager Eliza had hit some bumps after returning from Mexico, and days later they announced they had officially ended their engagement."Tricky emotions watching it all unfold," he wrote on Instagram December 2023. "We’re leading our amicable split with nothing but positivity and mutual respect for one another."

Status: SplitThough postpartum nurse Kylee Russell lamented boyfriend Aven Jones' unwillingness to get down on bended knee—a move he was purportedly prepared to make while romancing Bachelorette Rachel Recchia—she ultimately accepted Aven's Paradise proposal to "get out of here and make it work." Though that meant her planned engagement gown remained packed, "I just had to do what I felt was right," she said. "Love is all about taking risk."Two days after their December 2023 finale aired, she announced on her Instagram Stories that their relationship had "dissolved due to multiple infidelities." Aven later issued an apology to Kylee, writing, "I have made major mistakes in the relationship and hurt someone who was very close to me."

Status: Engaged"I am happy with how this season turns out!" Charity Lawson teased to E! News, a statement that way undersold her August 2023 finale. Dropping to one knee, integrative medicine specialist Dotun Olubeko proclaimed their love to be "perfect," asking the child and family therapist, "Would you do me the honor of turning this fairytale into a reality?"While their happily ever after awaits—the pair said they're considering a 2025 or 2026 wedding—the Georgia native will first take a spin through the Dancing With the Stars ballroom. "All right, baby," Dotun told Charity on The Bachelorette: After the Final Rose. "So I know you like to cut up, you like to dance and you like to get down. You know that we've talked about this—about how amazing this opportunity would be. And I am so happy to be the one to tell you that you're gonna be on Dancing With the Stars! Baby, let's go!"

Status: MarriedZach shall get his happy ending. Despite more than a few Fantasy Suite-related stumbles, Zach Shallcross ended season 27 in March 2023 down on one knee. "I am so in love with you," he told travel nurse Kaity Biggar. "You are my world. The love I feel for you is something I could have never imagined."In July 2023, the Texas-based duo made an even bigger step in their journey, with Kaity sharing on Instagram, "Officially roommates."

They wed on May 23, 2025, in what Kaity labeled "a cute little chapel celebration." Though they'd initially planned a larger affair, "I just took a step back, and I was like, 'I don't know if we need this,'" she explained on a June 2025 episode of the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast. "The whole point of a wedding is just staying true to the love and the connection of both of us, and I felt like I was honing in too much on little details."

But one key element left her charmed. The aunt who nominated her to compete for Zach's heart found the Austin-area chapel they used for their ceremony. Said Kaity, "It was perfect."

Status: SplitAh, Mom and Dad. Though they left BIP season seven hand-in-Neil-Lane-diamond-free-hand, Danielle Maltby, who lost her fiancé to a drug overdose years before she competed on Nick Viall's season, and single dad Michael Allio (he shares 7-year-old son James with his late wife) seemed slated for Bachelor Nation couple goals status.  But a year after Maltby relocated from Nashville to be with Allio in Ohio, he confirmed they'd split. "We both threw a lot into this relationship and it's really awful when it doesn't work out," Allio said on a September 2023 episode of Jason Tartick's Trading Secrets podcast. "When things don't work out, when you realize that love is there, but you're not necessarily compatible, you mourn the loss, not of just that person and that friend in your life, but also the future that you had envisioned."

Status: Split"I will love you until the end of time. I will love you until my last breath and I want to start forever with you," Brandon Jones proclaimed while proposing to "best friend" Serene Russell on season seven of Paradise. Alas, their journey was cut short. Five months after their engagement aired, Brandon (a runner-up on Michelle Young's season) and Serene (who romanced Clayton Echard) announced they had split in a joint May 2023 statement. "We have tried to work privately on our relationship which has been incredibly challenging in the public eye," they wrote on Instagram. "This has been immensely hard to accept and painful, as there is a lot of love between the two of us. We are deeply hurting and can only ask that there be no hate."

Status: SplitPilot Rachel's engagement to general contractor Tino Franco stalled when he kissed another woman while their 2022 season was still airing. "I do not stand by what I did at all," he said on The Viall Files. "It was not cool. It wasn't fair to Rachel, and it haunts me daily still. It's something I'm ashamed of and certainly wish I could have done it differently like a million times over."

Status: SplitWell, it was certainly a journey. Susie Evans initially rejected Bachelor Clayton Echard's overtures during the 2022 finale only to reunite with him off-camera...and then split once again six months later. But the L.A.-based videographer insists their breakup was for the right reasons. "The people around me could see that my sparkle had dulled and I was far from thriving," she wrote in a November 2022 post for her blog "Susie Was Like." She acknowledged they "had joyous moments often, but deep down I was struggling and felt misaligned with the best version of me."

Susie went on to date Bachelor Nation member Justin Glaze, before the couple announced they had broken up in August 2024.

Status: SplitMinnesota elementary school teacher Michelle accepted a Neil Lane sparkler from Texas-based sales exec Nayte Olukoya—and a $200,000 check from producers to put toward their future home. But, ultimately, the pair just didn't have the right foundation, announcing their breakup six months after their season's finale aired in December 2021. Though he said on The Viall Files, "There was lots of ups and downs, lots of arguments, lots of fights and just not really clicking, not really seeing eye-to-eye," Nayte acknowledged that not having that final split conversation in person was "a dick move."Michelle started dating Jack Leius in 2023, and they announced their engagement the following year. Their Minnesota vows took place in June 2025.

Status: SplitViewers fully got onboard with Maurissa Gunn and Riley Christian's vision of a future filled with sweet Sunday mornings. But ultimately the BIP season seven duo only got a couple dozen weekends together. "We have decided to go our separate ways," patient coordinator Maurissa (who romanced Peter Weber) and attorney Riley (one of Tayshia Adams' suitors) announced in a joint January 2022 statement. "Never did we imagine this, but we've come to a point where we both need to work on ourselves."

Bachelor Nation's first same-sex couple got engaged on season six of Bachelor in Paradise but announced their 2019 split on Halloween.

"What has always been at the forefront of our relationship is love and care for one another. Our priority is doing what is best for us. With a heavy heart full of love for one another we have decided it is best for us to take a step back from our relationship," they said in a joint statement posted on Instagram. "We ultimately want what is best for us in the long run and for us right now, that means being apart and growing individually."

Status: EngagedParadise lost? Not quite. Though Noah Erb and Abigail Heringer broke up in Mexico during the BIP's seventh season, they realized they could see forever in each other's eyes. Initially settling in San Diego, the travel nurse (who competed for Tayshia's heart) and the financial manager (who received Matt James' first impression rose) recently purchased a place in his hometown of Tulsa. "About to enter our Chip and Joanna Gaines era because your girl bought her very first house!!!" Abigail wrote on Instagram in July 2023. "Excited to start our next chapter and for all the memories we'll create here!!" Starting with a few wedding plans. Ahead of their move, Noah proposed at a beachfront San Diego home in August 2023.

Status: MarriedNever hurts to have a little practice run. While planning their September 2023 vows, Serena Pitt (a finalist on Matt James' season) and Joe Amabile (the Chicago grocery store owner who found fame after Becca Kufrin sent him home night one in 2018) decided to just do the damn thing at City Hall near their New York City digs, roughly one year after leaving Paradise engaged. "JUST MARRIED !!" Serena, now hosting the Bachelor Happy Hour podcast with her husband, captioned the October 2022 video. "We are still having a wedding this September but who doesn't want to get married twice!"

Status: Married"Mari, I am f--king so in love with you," boy band manager Kenny Braasch said as he slipped that Neil Lane diamond onto Mari Pepin's finger on the 2021 Paradise finale. "And I literally, like, I can't see my life without you." So the Maryland beauty queen, who initially charmed Bachelor Matt, moved to Kenny's native Chicago and set about planning their forever. And before she and Kenny (eliminated by Tayshia Adams in week five) wed in a 65-guest oceanfront ceremony in Puerto Rico in November 2023, they made their love permanent, getting inked with matching tattoos during a May 2023 trip to the Bahamas.

Former Bachelorette Becca and Thomas Jacobs (one of Katie Thurston's suitors) got together on Bachelor in Paradise season seven in 2021, broke up on the show, then reconciled after production wrapped. In May 2022, they announced they were engaged, and that Becca proposed. "I hope that other people can now feel empowered and say it's okay to bend the rules," she told E! News. The real estate agent returned the favor that October. In September 2023, the two welcomed their first child, son Benson. Wrote Becca on Instagram, "No amount of words can begin to capture the amount of love and awe we have over this tiny man."Though she's awfully fond of her 6-foot-6 guy as well. Weeks after bringing home Benson, the pair wed in a spontaneous Oct. 13 ceremony.

#898. Arsenal dig deep to earn WCL draw in face of Barcelona dominance

Arsenal continue to be a sharp thorn in the side of the European champions, Barcelona, and they dug deep to hold on to a draw at the Camp Nou on Thursday night. Frida Maanum put the Gunners ahead despite a hugely dominant performance from Barcelona, but Caroline Graham Hansen’s equaliser ensured the spoils would be shared.

Barcelona have been formidable when playing at the club’s main stadium, winning nine and drawing twice, against Chelsea in the semi-finals in 2023 and now Arsenal.

“Grit, resilience, discipline, clarity, communication, leadership, bravery – that’s a lot of words,” said Renée Slegers, whose side now lie fourth in the standings. “There’s a lot of really good things in this performance that we definitely want to build on.”

The last time these two teams met, Arsenal lifted the Champions League trophy at Barcelona’s expense after the most perfect defensive performance and a Stina Blackstenius goal in Lisbon in 2025. It was a far less perfect defensive performance this time but Arsenal showed the guts they have been missing at times this season, against the team that retook their crown last season, and showed they can play ugly when needed.

There was one change to the team that earned a 2-1 win against Liverpool on Sunday, but it was a significant one. Olivia Smith was replaced by Maanum and the Norwegian slotted into the No 10 role with Alessia Russo, who has scored 12 goals in nine games for club and country, moving into the centre-forward position.

It was the England forward’s play on the left that set up the shock first-half goal that temporarily silenced the crowd. She beat two and worked the ball to Maanum. Barcelona got the ball away but Russo was there again and delivered a perfect cross across the face of goal for Caitlin Foord. The Australian forced a close-range save from Cata Coll only for Maanum to power in the loose ball.

The pocket of travelling fans behind plexiglass in the upper tier were jubilant. About 1,000 had travelled despite the late switch of the match to Thursday due to a 24-hour general strike in Spain on Wednesday.

Benfica rebounded from their humbling defeat by Arsenal last time out to claim a second Women’s Champions League victory of the season by seeing off struggling Austria Vienna 3-1.

Beaten 3-0 at Meadow Park a fortnight ago following Alessia Russo’s hat-trick, Benfica had the ideal opportunity to get back to winning ways against a Vienna side who had picked up one point in three games.

They went ahead at Lisbon’s Estadio da Luz through Andreia Norton in the fifth minute before Carina Wenninger levelled after half-time when Valentina Potzl was upended in the area by Lena Pauels.

But Vienna goalkeeper Jasmin Pal’s 73rd-minute red card proved a turning point as Caroline Møller headed home before she teed up Nycole Raysla to score in time added on. Press Association

The goal came decidedly against the run of play but Barcelona struggled to capitalise on their first-half dominance. Ewa Pajor and Graham Hansen were particularly threatening as Barcelona targeted Arsenal’s left, made up of the less experienced Taylor Hinds and Lisa Baum.

The scoreline at the break was a little unfathomable based on the run of play and the domestic fortunes of both sides. While Arsenal languish in sixth in the WSL, 12 points behind the league leaders, Manchester City, Barcelona have won nine of their 10 games in Liga F, having scored 41 goals and built a five-point lead over their nearest rivals, Real Madrid.

Arsenal’s gameplan felt familiar. It was as if they had studied the blueprint religiously followed by teams that have sat back in a low block and frustrated them week-in, week-out in the WSL this season.

No topic is too small or too big for us to cover as we deliver a twice-weekly roundup of the wonderful world of women’s football

Aitana Bonmatí, the three-time Ballon d’Or winner, was surprisingly relegated to the bench but her arrival shortly before the hour elevated Barcelona’s threat, causing Arsenal’s defending to look even more calamitous at times, and lifted the mood in a frustrated stadium.

Three minutes after her arrival they were level. Esmee Brugts found an unmarked Graham Hansen on the right and she cut inside and swept in past Misa Rodríguez.

It was no surprise that Baum and Hinds, who had been run ragged, were removed soon after, with former Barcelona player Ona Batlle and Smith, Arsenal’s record signing, replacing them.

Arsenal were better after the goal and the changes, occasionally breaking free of their prison of a final third. At the end they were clinging on, but cling on they did.

“If we were to do it again, we’d try to stay on the ball for longer and play our game even more,” said Slegers. “Definitely there were moments in the first half and in the second half where we were really, really dangerous and created big chances, open chances. I’m just really pleased with the way we played the game tonight because it’s a very different game to what we usually play and that we can do it this way is a big boost for us as a team and that’s what we’re going to take with us going forward.”
